signal_or_failure: International sales FY1995

signal_or_failure: Eleven employees

signal_or_failure: Repeat purchase above 40% of orders

notes: Three prints of one sentence are one statement; the same company gave 60% seven months earlier and 44% six weeks later (U.48).

signal_or_failure: A distribution channel built out of other people's pages

signal_or_failure: One quarter exceeded the whole prior year

signal_or_failure: A competitor's legal attack lands three days before pricing

signal_or_failure: A firm-commitment offering completed 20% above the filed size and above the top of the range
what_it_demonstrated: That institutional buyers committed 54,000,000 dollars of primary risk capital to an unprofitable online bookseller with 256 employees

notes: Hindsight guard: nothing argues backwards to the rationality of a 1996 decision; the Series A trigger had already fixed a minimum deal size.

signal_or_failure: A counterparty's audited filing describes the same universe: 431 superstores and a 344000 sq ft DC stocking over 400000 titles and revenues 2448m

what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That either model was winning: the periods are not coterminous and B&N's prior year was a 52,976k net LOSS
notes: The only independent Tier-1 validation available and the only one that cuts against the company's framing (U.66 U.67 U.80).

signal_or_failure: External press attention sustained across the year
magnitude: at least six substantial national items, 1996-05-16 to 1997-01-05
what_it_demonstrated: That a 11-to-256 person company held national business-press interest through the whole stage, and was written about alongside Book Stacks, Wave, B&N and Borders
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Nothing about demand: every number the press carried was supplied by the company and it refused revenue figures in the same month
notes: Presence is evidenced and yield is not; no channel is attributed revenue anywhere (U.72).

signal_or_failure: Physical capacity contracted for three times over inside nine months

what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That the forecast was correct, that the space was sufficient, or that any of it was deliberate: no plan document or board minute survives
notes: The strongest non-financial evidence of intent in the stage: it is contractual rather than rhetorical (U.105).
